title: Etale splitting of an integral fibre with normal residue fields
statement:
Let $A\to D$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $D$ is integral over $A$ (every element satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$). Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset D$ be primes with inverse image $\mathfrak p$. Assume that there are finitely many primes of $D$ over $\mathfrak p$ and that for every such prime $\mathfrak r$, the extension $\kappa(\mathfrak r)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is algebraic and normal and has finite automorphism group over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; here $\kappa(\mathfrak r)=\operatorname{Frac}(D/\mathfrak r)$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$, and normal means that all minimal polynomials split. There exist an etale $A$-algebra $B$ (meaning $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]), a prime $\mathfrak p'\subset B$ over $\mathfrak p$, a prime $\mathfrak q'\subset D'=B\otimes_A D$ contracting to both $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p'$, and an isomorphism of $B$-algebras
$$D'\simeq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n,\qquad n\geq1,$$
such that each $D_j$ is integral over $B$ and has exactly one prime $\mathfrak q_j$ over $\mathfrak p'$, each $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)/\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is purely inseparable, and $\mathfrak q'$ is the prime of $D'$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q_1$. Purely inseparable means that in positive characteristic every element has some $p$-power in the base field, and in characteristic zero the extension is trivial. Tensor products are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with their usual algebra multiplication. No finite-dimensionality of the full residue extensions and no finite-generation assumption on $D$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, applied when residue extensions are normal with finite automorphism groups, as explicitly done in pione.tex, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, second reduction paragraph. Finiteness of their maximal separable subextensions follows from fields.tex Tag 0BR4 (lemma-normal-embeddings-differ-by-aut), Tag 09HJ (lemma-separable-degree), and Tag 030K (lemma-separable-first); the chosen prime is lifted through the nonzero tensor product of the two residue fields.

proof.text: Enumerate the finitely many primes $\mathfrak r_i$ of $D$ over $\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-dl-a1-normal-finite-aut-separable-subfield] to each normal algebraic extension $E_i=\kappa(\mathfrak r_i)$ of $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: its separable subfield $F_i$ is finite-dimensional. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable], $F_i/k$ is separable and $E_i/F_i$ is purely inseparable. This uses no finiteness of the full fields $E_i/k$.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, hypothesis (2), and pione.tex Tag 0BST, second reduction paragraph; field-theoretic justification by fields.tex Tags 0BME, 0BR4, 09HJ, 030K

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-integral-finite-residue-model] to these subfields. Obtain $A\to C\subseteq D$ finite over $A$, with $D$ integral over $C$, such that contraction is a bijection on primes above $\mathfrak p$. For $\mathfrak s_i=C\cap\mathfrak r_i$, put $L_i=\kappa(\mathfrak s_i)$. The same cited statement gives $[L_i:k]<\infty$ and pure inseparability of $E_i/L_i$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ satisfies both finite-fibre and finite-dimensional-residue hypotheses of the existing integral-fibre splitting theorem.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, construction of the finite intermediate algebra

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-fibre-etale-splitting] to $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\mathfrak p$. The affine etale neighbourhood has coordinate algebra $B$ and a prime $\mathfrak p'$ over $\mathfrak p$. The theorem gives a finite clopen affine partition of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C)$; write its factors as $C_j$. Each has a single fibre prime $\mathfrak t_j$ over $\mathfrak p'$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak t_j)/\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ purely inseparable. Here the affine-spectrum and integral-morphism conventions identify a finite ring map with the corresponding finite, hence integral, affine morphism. The tensor-product identification of this affine pullback, with both projections, is [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra].

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, applying finite-algebra etale splitting to S-prime

proof.text: Set $D'=B\otimes_A D$. It is integral over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], the clopen pieces correspond to idempotents. Disjointness makes their pairwise products zero, since those products are idempotents with empty distinguished open; their sum is then idempotent with distinguished open the whole spectrum, so equals $1$ by uniqueness. If $e_j\in B\otimes_A C$ are the idempotents of the finite clopen partition, map them to $D'$ and put $D_j=e_jD'$ (with identity $e_j$). Orthogonality and $\sum e_j=1$ give the explicit inverse ring homomorphisms $x\mapsto(e_jx)_j$ and $(x_j)_j\mapsto\sum x_j$. They are $B$-linear, so $D'\cong\prod_jD_j$ as $B$-algebras. Each factor is the quotient $D'/(1-e_j)$; mapping a monic integral equation into this quotient shows that $D_j$ is integral over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, final sentence: pull the finite-model product decomposition back to S; explicit orthogonal-idempotent calculation

proof.text: Fix $j$ and let $\mathfrak s_i$ be the image in $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $\mathfrak t_j$. By the fibre bijection of [lem-dl-a1-integral-finite-residue-model], exactly one original fibre prime maps to it, namely $\mathfrak r_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] over $C$, with $(B\otimes_AC)\otimes_CD\cong B\otimes_AD$, $\operatorname{Spec}D'=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AC)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\operatorname{Spec}D$, and $\operatorname{Spec}D_j$ is the part over $V_j$; so a prime of $D_j$ over $\mathfrak p'$ lies over $\mathfrak t_j$ and over a prime of $D$ above $\mathfrak s_i$, which is $\mathfrak r_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points], the primes of $D_j$ above $\mathfrak p'$ correspond to primes of $E_i\otimes_{L_i}\kappa(\mathfrak t_j)$. This tensor ring is nontrivial by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-tensor-nontrivial] and has a maximal, hence prime, ideal by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal]. For uniqueness, $\operatorname{Spec}E_i\to\operatorname{Spec}L_i$ is radicial: it is a one-point map and $E_i/L_i$ is purely inseparable. The equivalence in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] makes it universally injective, so its pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak t_j)$ is injective on points. Thus the tensor ring has exactly one prime, and $D_j$ has exactly one prime $\mathfrak q_j$ over $\mathfrak p'$.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, preservation of singleton fibres when pulling back from S-prime; schemes.tex Tag 01JT and morphisms.tex Tag 01S4

proof.text: The pullback of the field-spectrum map in the previous step is itself universally injective: any further base change is a base change of the same original map, by associativity of fibre products. By the converse equivalence in [def-weil-radicial-morphism], it is radicial, so its unique point has residue field purely inseparable over $\kappa(\mathfrak t_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field], that residue field is $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$ with the indicated field maps. Together with $\kappa(\mathfrak t_j)/\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ from step 3, this gives $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)/\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ purely inseparable: in characteristic $p>0$, if $a^{p^u}=b$ is in the intermediate field and $b^{p^v}$ is in the base, then $a^{p^{u+v}}$ is in the base; in characteristic zero both field maps are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, final residue-field assertion; schemes.tex Tag 01JT and morphisms.tex Tag 01S4; exponent computation written explicitly

proof.text: Finally lift the prescribed $\mathfrak q$, rather than just an unspecified fibre prime. The ring $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is nontrivial by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-tensor-nontrivial], and [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal] supplies a prime. Since $\operatorname{Spec}D'=\operatorname{Spec}D\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] gives a prime $\mathfrak q'$ of $D'$ contracting to $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p'$. A prime of a finite product contains all but exactly one of its factor idempotents: at most one survives because they are orthogonal, and at least one survives because their sum is $1$. Consequently $\mathfrak q'$ belongs to one factor. In particular the product has at least one factor. Permute the factors so this is $D_1$; step 5 makes its fibre prime $\mathfrak q_1$. This supplies every prescribed clause.
